traits.stamens.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 359: stamens 5 to 10, rarely 1 or many. Book writes ∞ (numerous); 200 is our stand-in for the upper bound and 20 for 'numerous' with no stated lower bound.

traits.carpels.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 359: carpels 1 to 3 or 5, rarely 12; typical 3 follows Floral Diagrams p. 232 (general formula G (1) 3-13).

traits.corolla_shape.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 359: usually 5 free petals. Free petals: rotate by PlantGen's free-petal rule; the book names no other corolla form.

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 359, 505: Simpson calls the flowers usually hypogynous. Simpson p. 505 defines hypogynous and epigynous as flowers without a hypanthium.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 218 Anacardiaceae: trees or shrubs, often with resinous bark; leaves alternate, very rarely opposite, simple or compound; no stipules (very rarely obscure ones); flowers bisexual or unisexual, mostly regular; petals 3 to 7, or none; stamens often twice the petals; ovary superior, mostly of one cell with one ovule; fruit mostly a drupe (mango, pistachio, sumac). The flowers bisexual or of one sex with bisexual ones on the same plant are read as hermaphrodite or polygamous.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Anacardiaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Blepharocaryaceae, Julianiaceae, Pistaciaceae, Podoaceae: how long the leaves last (character 37), coded often evergreen, often deciduous. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.
